children: Google DeepMind released AlphaGenome Atlas, a database that uses its AlphaGenome AI model to pre-calculate the predicted regulatory impact of all 9 billion possible single-letter changes to human DNA. The result is a 1-petabyte dataset, reachable through a web portal that requires no coding.

Scientists understand the 2% of the genome that codes for proteins relatively well and have limited knowledge of the remaining 98%. The Atlas introduces the AlphaGenome Variant Impact score, a single measure combining predictions for both, which lets researchers prioritize the most promising avenues without sifting through thousands of data points.

Two collaborators have results already. At the Broad Institute, Laura Covill's team used the score on unsolved rare disease cases and surfaced a variant in the DNM1 gene that the model predicted would create an incorrect splice site. Gareth Hawkes applied it to more than 54,000 UK Biobank participants and found 22% more non-coding genetic associations, along with 19 regions linked to body mass index.

title: Google DeepMind Maps All 9 Billion Human DNA Variants
